The petition was made by her father Francisco Figueroa on her behalf, the tract having been willed to her by her uncle Gen. Register correctly records the Mexican grantee and not the U.S.-era claimant Henry D. McCobb, who bought in through Jose de Arnaz in 1851 (claim petition stamped p4).

land_case.evidence: p1 red label 'CASE No. 359 SOUTHERN DISTRICT'; every transcript leaf stamped '359 SD'; PDF filename cubanc_lcf_sd359.pdf; District Court caption stamped p44 'Docket No. 359 / Transcript No. 170'. Board of Commissioners docket was 170, matching Hoffman's commission_no.

outcome.evidence: Board decree stamped p39 (filed 3 July 1855): 'it is adjudged by the Commission that the Claim is valid and it is therefore decreed that his application for a confirmation thereof be allowed ... called "Corral de Tierra" and contains one square league'. The United States appealed (AG notice 31 Dec 1855, stamped p42; U.S. petition for review stamped pp44-46) and then appealed again to the Supreme Court. Supreme Court decree No. 387, December Term 1864, entered 10 March 1865, stamped p74: 'it is now ordered, adjudged and decreed by this Court that the decree of the said District Court in this cause be and the same is hereby affirmed on the payment of costs in this Court by the appellee, but that on entering the decree herein the quantity of land to be surveyed within the exterior limits of the grant ... be restricted to one square league of land and no more'. District Court final decree, stamped pp78-79, 9 December 1865, so orders. Confirmation is final in the file.

notes: Single-volume file, 91 PDF images / 80 stamped transcript pages; image-to-stamp offset drifts from +4 to +11 across the file, so all evidence is cited by stamped page. Hoffman agrees on year, governor and grantee. One real ambiguity worth flagging: the Departmental committee report of 5 July 1836 and Governor Chico's testimonio of 14 July 1836 both describe the concession as made 'al Ciud.o Fran.co Figueroa' (stamped pp21-22), and McCobb's own District Court answer says Gutierrez 'made an order granting to said Francisco Figueroa for his said daughter Guadalupe' (stamped p50). The governor's decree itself, however, names the minor Guadalupe Figueroa as owner in fee, so the register's grantee is right on the grant document. The Supreme Court cut the confirmed quantity to one square league; the register carries no acreage field for this record beyond patent_acres, which Phase C checks.

notes: Single-volume file, 69 PDF images / 61 stamped transcript pages; image-to-stamp offset drifts from +4 to +8, so evidence is cited by stamped page. The claimant died in 1851 and the case was carried by his heirs; the District Court file carries a clerk's note (stamped p60) 'Claimant dead - no order reviving suit in name of heirs'.

notes: Single-volume file, 130 PDF images / 119 stamped transcript pages; image-to-stamp offset runs +5 early and +11 in the district-court section, so evidence is cited by stamped page. All graded fields agree with Hoffman. The confirmation became final by dismissal of the appeal rather than by a merits decree of the District Court, which is why the file has no District Court decree of confirmation; the operative decree is the Board's of 2 May 1854, made final 1856. Hoffman marks this rancho patented in 1862 and the register gives 28 Feb 1861; no patent copy is in the pages read, so patent fields are left for Phase C. Grant chain worth recording: Arguello permission 18 Apr 1823 and juridical possession 22 May 1823, an Alvarado addition of 2 Jan 1841, then Micheltorena's four-league grant of 1844 (claim petition stamped pp4-5; Abrego deposition stamped pp6-7).

name.evidence: p1 red label 'CASE No. 36 / NORTHERN DISTRICT / CANADA del CORTE de MADERA GRANT / MAXIMO MARTINEZ CLAIMANT'; transcript title leaf stamped p1 'for the place named Canada del Corte de Madera'; Board docket entry stamped p2 'for the Place named Canada del Corte de Madera'; grant translation stamped p21 'owner of the location designated "Canada del Corte de Madera"'; Board transmittal letter stamped p70 'for the place known by the name of Canada del Corte Madera'. Register 'El Corte De Madera' drops 'Canada del' and prefixes 'El'; the shortened form 'Corte de Madera' does appear once in the Board docket entry of 28 Feb 1853 (stamped p3), but 'El Corte de Madera' occurs nowhere in the file.

year.evidence: Micheltorena's title (titulo), Spanish, closing clause stamped p17: 'Dado en Monterrey a primero de Mayo de mil ochocientos cuarenta y cuatro. Manl. Michelltorena, Manl. Jimeno srio.' The underlying decree, translation stamped p21: 'Monterey April the 27th 1844 ... I hereby declare the Citizen Maximo Martinez owner of the location designated "Canada del Corte de Madera" ... of an area of three "sitios de ganado mayor"', with Micheltorena's marginal 'Approved, and let the patent be issued. Monterey April 27th 1844.' Register 1844 confirmed. IMPORTANT ANTECEDENT: the original one-league grant of 'la Canada del Corte de Madera' was made 10 June 1833 to Maximo Martinez AND Domingo Peralta jointly, approved by the Territorial Deputation 17 May 1834 under Jose Figueroa (translation stamped p22), Peralta ceding his half to Martinez 19 May 1834; the 1844 act is an augmentation of two more leagues that also re-granted the whole three as one title.

governor.evidence: Title heading, stamped p16: 'El Ciudadano Manl. Michelltorena, Gral. de Brigada del ejercito Mexicano, ayudante Gral. de la plana Mayor del mismo, Gobernador Gral. e Inspector del Depart.o de California'; translation stamped p23 'The Citizen Manuel Micheltorena, General of Brigade of the Mexican Army, Adjutant General of the Staff, Commandant General and Inspector of the Department of California'. Signed 'Manl. Michelltorena, Manl. Jimeno srio' (stamped p17). Jimeno appears as Secretary of State reporting 27 April 1844 (stamped p21). The 1833 antecedent grant was Figueroa's.

grantee.evidence: Title, stamped p16: 'Por cuanto el Ciud.no Maximo Martinez, ha pretendido para su beneficio personal y el de su familia el aumento de dos sitios de Ganado mayor a continuacion del que se le tiene concedido desde 10 de Junio de 1833 ... he venido en concederle el aumento referido'; decree translation stamped p21 'I hereby declare the Citizen Maximo Martinez owner of the location designated "Canada del Corte de Madera"'. Grantee and U.S.-era claimant are the same man (red label 'MAXIMO MARTINEZ CLAIMANT'). Domingo Peralta, co-grantee under the 1833 grant, petitioned the Board to contest Martinez's right on 14 Aug 1852 (docket stamped pp2-3, petition at stamped p30) but the claim was confirmed to Martinez.

notes: Single-volume file, 214 PDF images / 207 stamped transcript pages; image-to-stamp offset runs about +4 early and +7 in the Board decision section, so evidence is cited by stamped page. This is the chunk's one substantive ERR. The register has almost certainly collapsed two generations: Manuel Nieto's c.1784 Fages concession of the whole 300,000-acre Nieto tract, and the 1834 Figueroa partition that carved it into Santa Gertrudes, Los Coyotes, Los Alamitos, Las Bolsas and Los Cerritos and issued a separate title to each heir. If the register's intent is the ORIGINAL concessionaire, then its year (1834) and governor (Figueroa) are the wrong pair for that man; if its intent is the 1834 grant, the grantee must be Juan Jose Nieto. Hoffman's 1862 table leaves both governor and grantee blank for this claim, so it offers no cross-check. Chain thereafter: Juan Jose Nieto sold to Juan Bautista Leandry 25 Jan 1840 (opinion stamped p119); Leandry died intestate and childless Dec 1843; half went to his widow Francisca Uribe (later O'Campo) as community property, half to his mother Ana Maria Testa, whose attorney Antonio Jose Cot sold it to Andres Pico 4 Mar 1850 (opinion stamped p120). Confirmed area ten square leagues; register patent 9 Mar 1875 is a Phase C check.

notes: Single-volume file, 66 PDF images / 58 stamped transcript pages; image-to-stamp offset runs +5 early and +8 at the end, so evidence is cited by stamped page. Hoffman's 1862 table leaves year, governor and grantee blank for this claim, so it offers no cross-check, but the case file settles all three exactly as the register has them and the District Court decree of Dec Term 1856 states them in one sentence (stamped p54). The register's parenthetical '(Maria Antonia De La Guerra Y Lataillade)' is the U.S.-era claimant used as a disambiguator, correctly kept out of the grantee field. Two points for a re-reader: the confirmation is capped at five square leagues and no more (stamped pp54-55), and the grant was made on the express condition of Departmental Assembly approval, which the committee of vacant lands gave only on 12 June 1846 on Ignacio del Valle's application as executor of the deceased Rojo (stamped pp16-17).
